S.FORM: tia=kari=maku ia, tia=ku pu-isua Kanakanavu miana ni-m-uru-ʔucaŋ tamu.
S.PHON: tiakarimaku ia tiaku puisua kanakanavu miana nimuruʔuʦaŋ tamu
S.FORM: tiakarimaku ia, tiaku puisua Kanakanavu miana nimuru'ucang tamu.
S.PHON: tiaka[r|ɾ]imaku ia tiaku puisua kanakanavu miana nimu[r|ɾ]uʔuʦaŋ tamu
S.TRANSL: I shall talk about the story of a Kanakanavu ancestor who was married to a snake, a hundred-pacer.

S.FORM: ni-mu-ca=kani sua cau-ini mu-usa na karanana tanasa-an pu-nannakə.
S.PHON: nimuʦakani sua ʦauini muusa na karanana tanasaan punannakə
S.FORM: nimucakani sua cauini muusa na karanana tanasaan punannake.
S.PHON: nimuʦakani sua ʦauini muusa na ka[r|ɾ]anana tanasaan punannake
S.TRANSL: His (i.e., the snake's) clansman had gone to a different tribe to arrange a marriage (for the snake).

S.FORM: ni-ala-avici=kan=kiai sua tia=ʔanai-ini sua ŋanai ia, ʔusu=kani sua ŋanai.
S.PHON: niaɾaavitʂikankiai sua tiaʔanaiini sua ŋanai ia ʔusukani sua ŋanai
S.FORM: niaraavicikankiai sua tia'anaiini sua nganai ia, 'usukani sua nganai.
S.PHON: nia[r|ɾ]aavitʂikankiai sua tiaʔanaiini sua ŋanai ia ʔusukani sua ŋanai
S.TRANSL: (The girl) he had brought back to be his relative was called (lit., whose name was) 'Usu.

S.FORM: ʔaisi=kan=cu na ca-canə, pu-kari-kari=kan sua sisiin, "calai=kia cu-cuulu ʔusu, tia=m-uru-ʔucaŋ tamu," misa=kan sua sisiin.
S.PHON: ʔaiʂikanʦu na ʦaʦanə pukarikarikan sua ʂiʂiin ʦaɾaikia ʦuʦuuɾu ʔusu tiamuruʔuʦaŋ tamu misakan sua ʂiʂiin
S.FORM: 'aisikancu na cacane, pukarikarikan sua sisiin, "caraikia cucuuru 'usu, tiamuru'ucang tamu," misakan sua sisiin.
S.PHON: ʔaiʂikanʦu na ʦaʦane puka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]ikan sua ʂiʂiin ʦa[r|ɾ]aikia ʦuʦuu[r|ɾ]u ʔusu tiamu[r|ɾ]uʔuʦaŋ tamu misakan sua ʂiʂiin
S.TRANSL: On their way (home), a sisiin (a traditional bird of omen) spoke, "I really pity 'Usu, who will marry a snake," thus said the sisiin.

S.FORM: pu-kari-kari=kani=cu ʔusu, "anaka naini kari tapinaŋai iisua, kaʔan=ku a-manəŋ ʔinia t<um>imana, aaka kari-ini" misa=kan sua ʔusu.
S.PHON: pukarikarikaniʦu ʔusu anaka naini kari tapinaŋai iisua kaʔanku amanəŋ ʔinia tumimana aaka kariini misakan sua ʔusu
S.FORM: pukarikarikanicu 'usu, "anaka naini kari tapinangai iisua, ka'anku amaneng 'inia t<um>imana, aaka kariini" misakan sua 'usu.
S.PHON: puka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]ikaniʦu ʔusu anaka naini ka[r|ɾ]i tapinaŋai iisua kaʔanku amaneŋ ʔinia tumimana aaka ka[r|ɾ]iini misakan sua ʔusu
S.TRANSL: 'Usu said, "What on earth did this bird say? I do not quite understand it (lit., I do not hear it clearly). What it said is bad," thus said 'Usu.

S.FORM: "kaʔan alinamaun tapinaŋai sian, masi-raru maamia si-pu-kari-kari-ini," misa=kan sua tia=ʔanai-ini.
S.PHON: kaʔan aɾinamaun tapinaŋai ʂian maʂiraru maamia ʂipukarikariini misakan sua tiaʔanaiini
S.FORM: "ka'an arinamaun tapinangai sian, masiraru maamia sipukarikariini," misakan sua tia'anaiini.
S.PHON: kaʔan a[r|ɾ]inamaun tapinaŋai ʂian maʂi[r|ɾ]a[r|ɾ]u maamia ʂipuka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]iini misakan sua tiaʔanaiini
S.TRANSL: "Birds here are not to be trusted. It's just the way they speak," thus said her relative-to-be.

S.FORM: makasua=kani=cu mu-caan mu-tanasə.
S.PHON: makasuakaniʦu muʦaan mutanasə
S.FORM: makasuakanicu mucaan mutanase.
S.PHON: makasuakaniʦu muʦaan mutanase
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, they went home.

S.FORM: tia=kani=cu k<um>a-kaənə, pu-kari-kari=kani ka-vaŋvaŋ cani piniŋa, "k<um>aən-a=cu lavai," misa=kani ka-vaŋvaŋ.
S.PHON: tiakaniʦu kumakaənə pukarikarikani kavaŋvaŋ ʦani piniŋa kumaənaʦu ɾavai misakani kavaŋvaŋ
S.FORM: tiakanicu k<um>akaene, pukarikarikani kavangvang cani pininga, "k<um>aenacu ravai," misakani kavangvang.
S.PHON: tiakaniʦu kumakaene puka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]ikani kavaŋvaŋ ʦani piniŋa kumaenaʦu [r|ɾ]avai misakani kavaŋvaŋ
S.TRANSL: (When it was time) to eat, the entire family spoke, "Eat now, lavai!" thus said everybody.

S.FORM: pa-cəpə-cəpəŋ=kan sua ʔusu, "anaka ʔaisi nanu sua tia=laʔəvə=ta?" misa-ən lavai maamia ka-vaŋvaŋ misa=kan sua ʔusu.
S.PHON: paʦəpəʦəpəŋkan sua ʔusu anaka ʔaiʂi nanu sua tiaɾaʔəvəta misaən ɾavai maamia kavaŋvaŋ misakan sua ʔusu
S.FORM: pacepecepengkan sua 'usu, "anaka 'aisi nanu sua tiara'eveta?" misaen ravai maamia kavangvang misakan sua 'usu.
S.PHON: paʦepeʦepeŋkan sua ʔusu anaka ʔaiʂi nanu sua tia[r|ɾ]aʔeveta misaen [r|ɾ]avai maamia kavaŋvaŋ misakan sua ʔusu
S.TRANSL: 'Usu thought, "Where on earth is my future husband?" All my relatives just said to me.

S.FORM: "taka-ʔunuŋ-a lavai," misa=kan sua cucuma-ini sua cau-piniŋa.
S.PHON: takaʔunuŋa ɾavai misakan sua ʦuʦumaini sua ʦaupiniŋa
S.FORM: "taka'ununga ravai," misakan sua cucumaini sua caupininga.
S.PHON: takaʔunuŋa [r|ɾ]avai misakan sua ʦuʦumaini sua ʦaupiniŋa
S.TRANSL: "Help yourself, lavai!" The rest of the family said (to her).

S.FORM: ala-sələcə=kan sua tamu ʔaisi=kan na virua "taka-ʔunuŋ-a, ʔusu," misa=kan.
S.PHON: aɾasəɾəʦəkan sua tamu ʔaiʂikan na virua takaʔunuŋa ʔusu misakan
S.FORM: araserecekan sua tamu 'aisikan na virua "taka'ununga, 'usu," misakan.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]ase[r|ɾ]eʦekan sua tamu ʔaiʂikan na vi[r|ɾ]ua takaʔunuŋa ʔusu misakan
S.TRANSL: The snake came out from a straw box, "Help yourself, 'Usu!" It said.

S.FORM: makasua=kan sua ʔusu məsə-ʔərəcə.
S.PHON: makasuakan sua ʔusu məsəʔərəʦə
S.FORM: makasuakan sua 'usu mese'erece.
S.PHON: makasuakan sua ʔusu meseʔe[r|ɾ]eʦe
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, 'Usu jumped to her feet and was scared stiff.

S.FORM: araanai=cu mia-sua, aaka=cu cəpəŋə.
S.PHON: araanaiʦu miasua aakaʦu ʦəpəŋə
S.FORM: araanaicu miasua, aakacu cepenge.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]aanaiʦu miasua aakaʦu ʦepeŋe
S.TRANSL: Since that time, she felt bad.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: "tia=ci=kia=ʔai=kusa ma-kai-nanu, tia=ava=ʔai laʔəv=aku sua tamu iisua, ma-naasə," misa=kan sua cəpəŋ-in.
S.PHON: tiatʂikiaʔaikusa makainanu tiaavaʔai ɾaʔəvaku sua tamu iisua manaasə misakan sua ʦəpəŋin
S.FORM: "tiacikia'aikusa makainanu, tiaava'ai ra'evaku sua tamu iisua, manaase," misakan sua cepengin.
S.PHON: tiatʂikiaʔaikusa makainanu tiaavaʔai [r|ɾ]aʔevaku sua tamu iisua manaase misakan sua ʦepeŋin
S.TRANSL: "What am I going to do? Could it be that the snake will indeed be my husband?" Thus, the girl may have been thinking (lit., her mind may have said).

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: "tia=ci=kia=ʔai=kusa ma-kai-nanu, tia=ava=ʔai laʔəv=aku sua tamu iisua, ma-naasə," misa=kan sua cəpəŋ-ini.
S.PHON: tiatʂikiaʔaikusa makainanu tiaavaʔai ɾaʔəvaku sua tamu iisua manaasə misakan sua ʦəpəŋini
S.FORM: "tiacikia'aikusa makainanu, tiaava'ai ra'evaku sua tamu iisua, manaase," misakan sua cepengini.
S.PHON: tiatʂikiaʔaikusa makainanu tiaavaʔai [r|ɾ]aʔevaku sua tamu iisua manaase misakan sua ʦepeŋini
S.TRANSL: "What am I going to do? Could it be that the snake will indeed be my husband?" Thus, the girl may have been thinking (lit., her mind may have said).

S.FORM: makasua=kani=cu um-aʔaru=kani=cu rua-vana, um-aʔaru=kani=cu ma-pitəʔə, tia=kani=cu si-ʔicəpə.
S.PHON: makasuakaniʦu umaʔarukaniʦu ruavana umaʔarukaniʦu mapitəʔə tiakaniʦu ʂiʔiʦəpə
S.FORM: makasuakanicu uma'arukanicu ruavana, uma'arukanicu mapite'e, tiakanicu si'icepe.
S.PHON: makasuakaniʦu umaʔa[r|ɾ]ukaniʦu [r|ɾ]uavana umaʔa[r|ɾ]ukaniʦu mapiteʔe tiakaniʦu ʂiʔiʦepe
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, it was getting slowly late in the evening; it was getting slowly dark. (It was time to go) to sleep.

S.FORM: "si-ʔicəp-a=cu kəəcə, lavai," misa=kan sua ʔanai-ini.
S.PHON: ʂiʔiʦəpaʦu kəəʦə ɾavai misakan sua ʔanaiini
S.FORM: "si'icepacu keece, ravai," misakan sua 'anaiini.
S.PHON: ʂiʔiʦepaʦu keeʦe [r|ɾ]avai misakan sua ʔanaiini
S.TRANSL: "Please sleep now, lavai." Her relatives said (to her).

S.FORM: si-ʔicəpə=kani sua ʔusu, ala-sulusulu=kani sua tamu mu-kusa na ta-tarə kuli-səʔələ=kan sua tamu.
S.PHON: ʂiʔiʦəpəkani sua ʔusu aɾasuɾusuɾukani sua tamu mukusa na tatarə kuɾisəʔəɾəkan sua tamu
S.FORM: si'icepekani sua 'usu, arasurusurukani sua tamu mukusa na tatare kurise'erekan sua tamu.
S.PHON: ʂiʔiʦepekani sua ʔusu a[r|ɾ]asu[r|ɾ]usu[r|ɾ]ukani sua tamu mukusa na tata[r|ɾ]e ku[r|ɾ]iseʔe[r|ɾ]ekan sua tamu
S.TRANSL: As 'Usu slept, the snake approached the bed slowly and stretched itself out.

S.FORM: makasua=cu sua ʔusu mata-riŋətən-a. kaʔan k<um>a-kaən caan=kan cainana, kaʔan k<um>a-kaən ka-paipai=kan=cu maamia cuʔuan si kaʔan=cu k<um>a-kaən.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu sua ʔusu matariŋətəna kaʔan kumakaən ʦaankan ʦainana kaʔan kumakaən kapaipaikanʦu maamia ʦuʔuan ʂi kaʔanʦu kumakaən
S.FORM: makasuacu sua 'usu mataringetena. ka'an k<um>akaen caankan cainana, ka'an k<um>akaen kapaipaikancu maamia cu'uan si ka'ancu k<um>akaen.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu sua ʔusu mata[r|ɾ]iŋetena kaʔan kumakaen ʦaankan ʦainana kaʔan kumakaen kapaipaikanʦu maamia ʦuʔuan ʂi kaʔanʦu kumakaen
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, 'Usu became skinny. She did not eat for one year, she did not eat anything, and she was all bones because she did not eat.

S.FORM: pa-cəpə-cəpəŋə=kani sua caan piniŋa, "tia=kusa pakai-nanu kaʔan=ʔai tia=um-a-ʔarau ara-aaka ʔusu maka-sia kaʔan=cu k<um>a-kaənə, ka-paipai=cu maamia cuʔuan."
S.PHON: paʦəpəʦəpəŋəkani sua ʦaan piniŋa tiakusa pakainanu kaʔanʔai tiaumaʔarau araaaka ʔusu makaʂia kaʔanʦu kumakaənə kapaipaiʦu maamia ʦuʔuan
S.FORM: pacepecepengekani sua caan pininga, "tiakusa pakainanu ka'an'ai tiauma'arau araaaka 'usu makasia ka'ancu k<um>akaene, kapaipaicu maamia cu'uan."
S.PHON: paʦepeʦepeŋekani sua ʦaan piniŋa tiakusa pakainanu kaʔanʔai tiaumaʔa[r|ɾ]au a[r|ɾ]aaaka ʔusu makaʂia kaʔanʦu kumakaene kapaipaiʦu maamia ʦuʔuan
S.TRANSL: The whole family thought, "What is to be done? Isn't 'Usu going to get even worse and worse the way she is not eating and is all bones?"

S.FORM: "tia=kita cukui ma-kari-kari, ma-manəŋ cukui. nuu mu-a-kusa=kasu, nuu mata-ili=kasu" kisa-ən=kiai tamu.
S.PHON: tiakita ʦukui makarikari mamanəŋ ʦukui nuu muakusakasu nuu mataiɾikasu kisaənkiai tamu
S.FORM: "tiakita cukui makarikari, mamaneng cukui. nuu muakusakasu, nuu matairikasu" kisaenkiai tamu.
S.PHON: tiakita ʦukui maka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]i mamaneŋ ʦukui nuu muakusakasu nuu matai[r|ɾ]ikasu kisaenkiai tamu
S.TRANSL: "We may talk (it) over. What do you think if you go, if you undergo a transformation?" They said to the snake.

S.FORM: makasua=kan=cu sua ʔanai-ini, "ta-a=pa kəəcə ʔuma-ʔuma, lavai," misa=kan.
S.PHON: makasuakanʦu sua ʔanaiini taapa kəəʦə ʔumaʔuma ɾavai misakan
S.FORM: makasuakancu sua 'anaiini, "taapa keece 'uma'uma, ravai," misakan.
S.PHON: makasuakanʦu sua ʔanaiini taapa keeʦe ʔumaʔuma [r|ɾ]avai misakan
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, her relatives said, "Go to the fields, if you please."

S.FORM: mu-caanə=kani=cu mu-a-kusa ʔusu ki-papa ʔanai-ini, ʔacu=ava=kan ala-cini mu-a-kusa nuŋnuŋ sua tamu.
S.PHON: muʦaanəkaniʦu muakusa ʔusu kipapa ʔanaiini ʔaʦuavakan aɾatʂini muakusa nuŋnuŋ sua tamu
S.FORM: mucaanekanicu muakusa 'usu kipapa 'anaiini, 'acuavakan aracini muakusa nungnung sua tamu.
S.PHON: muʦaanekaniʦu muakusa ʔusu kipapa ʔanaiini ʔaʦuavakan a[r|ɾ]atʂini muakusa nuŋnuŋ sua tamu
S.TRANSL: As 'Usu followed her relatives (to the field), the snake indeed went alone to the stream.

S.FORM: ni-mu-kusa=kan nuŋnuŋ ŋapakuica.
S.PHON: nimukusakan nuŋnuŋ ŋapakuiʦa
S.FORM: nimukusakan nungnung ngapakuica.
S.PHON: nimukusakan nuŋnuŋ ŋapakuiʦa
S.TRANSL: It had gone to a stream called Ngapakuica.

S.FORM: mu-a-kusa=kan ʔinia pasi-kə-təvə sua rian-ini, cau=kani=cu.
S.PHON: muakusakan ʔinia paʂikətəvə sua rianini ʦaukaniʦu
S.FORM: muakusakan 'inia pasiketeve sua rianini, caukanicu.
S.PHON: muakusakan ʔinia paʂiketeve sua [r|ɾ]ianini ʦaukaniʦu
S.TRANSL: (When) it arrived there, it dropped its molt and cut itself in half, and a man (it had become).

S.FORM: pasi-kə-sanvari rian-in cau=cu, cau=cu cu-cuulu, cau ma-manəŋ, ni-marumanəŋ.
S.PHON: paʂikəsanvari rianin ʦauʦu ʦauʦu ʦuʦuuɾu ʦau mamanəŋ nimarumanəŋ
S.FORM: pasikesanvari rianin caucu, caucu cucuuru, cau mamaneng, nimarumaneng.
S.PHON: paʂikesanva[r|ɾ]i [r|ɾ]ianin ʦauʦu ʦauʦu ʦuʦuu[r|ɾ]u ʦau mamaneŋ nima[r|ɾ]umaneŋ
S.TRANSL: As it turned one half (of its body) inside out, it became a man, a real man, a good handsome man.

S.FORM: tia=kan=cu tu-ruru-vana.
S.PHON: tiakanʦu tururuvana
S.FORM: tiakancu tururuvana.
S.PHON: tiakanʦu tu[r|ɾ]u[r|ɾ]uvana
S.TRANSL: It was nearly dark in the evening.

S.FORM: pu-kari-kari=kan sua ʔanai-ini, "lavai mu-caan-a=cu=kita kəəcə, ru-vana-n=cu."
S.PHON: pukarikarikan sua ʔanaiini ɾavai muʦaanaʦukita kəəʦə ruvananʦu
S.FORM: pukarikarikan sua 'anaiini, "ravai mucaanacukita keece, ruvanancu."
S.PHON: puka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]ikan sua ʔanaiini [r|ɾ]avai muʦaanaʦukita keeʦe [r|ɾ]uvananʦu
S.TRANSL: Her relatives said, "Let's leave now, lavai, if you please. It's already dark in the evening."

S.FORM: mu-caan=kan=cu ma-kaasi ca-canə, pu-kari-kari sua ʔanai-ini, "ma-lavai ʔusu, pusu-alal-a=kita ca-canə ʔuuna cukui cau ca-canə na ta-tupuru-a."
S.PHON: muʦaankanʦu makaaʂi ʦaʦanə pukarikari sua ʔanaiini maɾavai ʔusu pusuaɾaɾakita ʦaʦanə ʔuuna ʦukui ʦau ʦaʦanə na tatupurua
S.FORM: mucaankancu makaasi cacane, pukarikari sua 'anaiini, "maravai 'usu, pusuararakita cacane 'uuna cukui cau cacane na tatupurua."
S.PHON: muʦaankanʦu makaaʂi ʦaʦane puka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]i sua ʔanaiini ma[r|ɾ]avai ʔusu pusua[r|ɾ]a[r|ɾ]akita ʦaʦane ʔuuna ʦukui ʦau ʦaʦane na tatupu[r|ɾ]ua
S.TRANSL: (As) they came to the road, her relatives spoke, "Lavai 'Usu, let's search the road to see if a man is to be found at the resting place by the roadside."

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: tara-kusa=kan na ta-tupuru-a muruʔana nannakə iisua, pu-kari-kari=kan ʔusu, "anaka naini ta-tupuru-a iisa ni-ma-tikuru kanasiaŋ, ma-takuisi=kan takuisi t<in>apas-a."
S.PHON: tarakusakan na tatupurua muruʔana nannakə iisua pukarikarikan ʔusu anaka naini tatupurua iisa nimatikuru kanaʂiaŋ matakuiʂikan takuiʂi tinapasa
S.FORM: tarakusakan na tatupurua muru'ana nannake iisua, pukarikarikan 'usu, "anaka naini tatupurua iisa nimatikuru kanasiang, matakuisikan takuisi t<in>apasa."
S.PHON: ta[r|ɾ]akusakan na tatupu[r|ɾ]ua mu[r|ɾ]uʔana nannake iisua puka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]ikan ʔusu anaka naini tatupu[r|ɾ]ua iisa nimatiku[r|ɾ]u kanaʂiaŋ matakuiʂikan takuiʂi tinapasa
S.TRANSL: The married woman looked toward the resting place and 'Usu said, "Who on earth is (the man) at the resting place, dressed in a red suit and a designer fur coat (over it)?"

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: tara-kusa=kan na ta-tupuru-a muruʔana nannakə iisua, pu-kari-kari=kan ʔusu, "anaka naini ʔaisi na ta-tupuru-a iisa ni-ma-tikuru kanasiaŋ, ma-takuisi=kan takuisi t<in>apas-a."
S.PHON: tarakusakan na tatupurua muruʔana nannakə iisua pukarikarikan ʔusu anaka naini ʔaiʂi na tatupurua iisa nimatikuru kanaʂiaŋ matakuiʂikan takuiʂi tinapasa
